INSIGHT: You can feel an emotion fully without reacting to it. These are separate things. Most people think feeling = reacting.

BEFORE: Ned had one mode — emotional blunting (System 2 intercepting every feeling before it registered). Zero practice with the feel-without-react pattern.

AFTER: Practiced this for first time with the manipulative friend situation — held frame, she cancelled because she 'couldn't handle me not reacting.' The technique working without even meeting.

SECOND INSIGHT — System 2 throttle: Ned's System 2 can't keep up with his speaking speed when he talks fast. So he DELIBERATELY slows himself down to half-speed in normal conversation so System 2 can intercept and steer. The fast talking is unmasked him. The normal pace is a governor.

THIRD INSIGHT — Causal chain: Trauma → emotional blunting as coping → ADHD masked by easy school → now needs to perform AND feel → falls back to blunting. ADHD is layered on top of trauma response, not just ADHD alone.

ON EMOTIONS GENERALLY:
- Identity emotions (shame, pride, guilt) — accessible
- Reward emotions (joy, desire, excitement) — need dopamine, mostly offline until meds
- Feel → name it → choose response (express, channel, sit, act) — not everything needs action
- Most emotions peak and fade in ~90 seconds if not fed with thoughts

Favorite mode discovered: curiosity about emotions — 'what IS this feeling?' — not analysis (which kills the feeling) but genuine interest that keeps it alive
